_README: Every callback seam that is CALLED through a NULL check and filled by
nobody needs a row here. tools/seam_audit.py measures the set; the
source-tools test refuses a seam that is empty and unledgered, and also
a row here for a seam that is no longer empty -- so a wiring cannot
leave a stale excuse behind, and a new empty seam cannot appear
unnoticed.
The point is not that every seam must be wired. Plenty stand for
drawing this port has no renderer for. The point is that leaving one
empty has to be a decision somebody wrote down, because an unwired seam
is invisible: the call compiles, runs, does nothing, and reads exactly
like working code. Six separate findings this cycle were that shape.
verdicts:
display   - object/DMA drawing; this port has no renderer
hardware  - talks to the cabinet (CMOS clock, DIPs, I/O)
fallback  - the call sites run the real routine in an else
unreached - the caller itself is not on a live path
deferred  - real, wireable, and not yet done; the note says what is
known and what still has to be established
`check` -- the mechanical premise under a verdict, so the verdict
cannot rot the way a prose note can. Every `unreached` and
`fallback` row carries one, and
test_every_ledger_verdict_premise_still_holds re-measures it:
fallback-else   every call site of the seam is followed by the
named routine in an else, so the real translation
runs when the seam is empty
no-src-caller   nothing in src/ calls the named entry point,
and src/ still defines it -- so the claim is
measuring a symbol that exists rather than
passing on a name that has been renamed away
guarded-by-test the claim is measured by the named test instead
This exists because a reachability claim went stale twice in one
cycle: WM_PMODE_HEADHELD stopped being unreachable the moment
mode_chokehold was translated, and wlvoice.py's exclusion of the
rope tables rested on a layer that had since been written. Both
were prose. A verdict nobody can re-measure is an excuse with a
shelf life.

read_clock.note: The CMOS real-time clock the time-and-date screen reads. There is no clock chip here, and inventing a time would make the screen lie.

time_date_dip_enabled.note: The operator DIP that enables the time-and-date screen. No switch bank to read; the screen it gates is display anyway.

remap_io.note: REMAP_IO, the cabinet's I/O address window, which the attract path reopens around the screens that touch hardware directly. There is no memory-mapped I/O window on this machine to remap, so the call has nothing to stand for.

music_adjustment_nonzero.note: The operator's music volume adjustment, read out of CMOS by the attract adapter to decide whether to play music at all. No adjustment store and no CMOS here; a default would be the cabinet's setting invented rather than read.

pal_getf.note: pal_getf, a palette allocation. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

screen_flash.note: the full-screen flash. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

shadow_trail.note: the shadow trail a moving object leaves. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

impact.note: the impact sprite a landed blow spawns. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

flash_white.note: flash_white's QDMAN fill of the whole screen. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

restore_hit_render_state.note: putting the palette back after a hit flash. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

keep_attached.note: WRESTLE.ASM keep_attached. Not a hole: every call site reads `if (c && c->keep_attached) ... else (void)wm_arcade_keep_attached(a);`, so the real translated routine runs when the seam is empty. All EIGHT call sites were checked -- the seven shared dispatchers and Bret's own, which the note used to leave out of its count. `check` re-measures them rather than asking anyone to take this sentence's word for it. The seam exists so a backend CAN take it over, not because anything is missing.

auto_pin_check.note: A field of wm_arcade_move_wrestler's callback set (wm/arcade/wm_arcade_move_dispatch.h). That routine is the FAITHFUL translation of WRESTLE.ASM's move_wrestler and is called only from a test; the live loop calls wm_arcade_move_ported_wrestler, its last step alone. Why the split exists and what it would take to collapse it -- deciding whether SPECIAL_MOVE_ADDR carries an id or an address for everybody -- is recorded under `auto_pin` in port/translation_manifest.json. auto_pin_check itself IS translated and IS called live, from match.c, where the source calls it.

resolve_label_token.note: With start_special_label, the two halves of the six shared dispatchers' startsp(). THE QUESTION THIS ROW CARRIED IS ANSWERED, and the answer is that most of the callers were a MISTRANSLATION rather than a missing implementation. The row previously asked whether startsp() being inert mattered; the next pass established that it IS reached from check_secret_moves, and this one read what the source actually does at those call sites. Every one of them ends in `calla change_anim1a` and never touches SPECIAL_MOVE_ADDR: DOINK.ASM:583 #scrt_hiptoss is `FACE24 dnk,hiptoss_anim / calla change_anim1a / WRSND W_DOINK,HIPTOSS_T1,PUNCH_T2`, and the other five are the same shape. So the fifteen secret-move call sites are gone -- replaced by the animation and sound the source plays -- and what is left is ONE caller per file, in fire_monitor, where the label comes from the wrestler's smove table rather than a literal. That one is genuinely about SPECIAL_MOVE_ADDR, and it is UNREACHED: wm_arcade_port_fire_monitor has no caller AT ALL -- not in src/ and not in tests, which the note used to say. What the tests call is the eight per-wrestler wm_arcade_<name>_fire_monitor bodies directly; the profile-driven front door above them is reached by nothing. The live monitor path is match_tick_smoves_for, a second translation of the same routines built from tools/wlsmove.py's generated tables, and it starts the animation itself. The id-versus-address decision recorded under `auto_pin` still stands, and it is now the only thing behind these two seams -- not fifteen moves that fire and do nothing.

unhandled_reaction.note: A port-INVENTED diagnostic, not a source routine: REACT1's dispatcher calls it when handed a reaction its own chunk does not cover. The note used to read 'diagnostic rather than behaviour. Worth filling with a counter so the number is measured instead of assumed.' The number is measured now, and it is ZERO. The live chain is wm_arcade_react123456789_reaction_callback -- all nine REACT files -- and driving every value of wm_arcade_reaction_id_t through it leaves nothing over: 52 enum members, ids 0 through 51, all claimed. The seam can only fire for a value outside the enum, which no caller produces. So it is unreached rather than deferred, and test_every_reaction_id_is_handled_by_the_chain holds it there -- a counter would have reported the same zero without saying why.

play_wrestler_tune.note: LIFEBAR.ASM:3003 DO_RIGHT_MUSIC, and this is the one deferred note that was SUBSTANTIALLY RIGHT -- the rest of this list was not, so it is worth saying which. It said the tune id is already resolved and what is missing is playing it. Both true. The correction is only to the size of the thing: it is not 'the DCS tune path' but five instructions -- `MOVK 1,A0 / MOVE A0,@MUSIC_HAP`, then #wrestler_tunes[WRESTLERNUM] (`.word 5,2,1,7,6,4,8,0,3`) into A3 and one `calla SNDSND`. DO_RIGHT_MUSIC is DO_RIGHT_MUSIC2 with a SLEEP 55 in front, which is the only difference between them. What genuinely blocks it: the seam belongs to wmania_attract_adapter, whose owner has no music sink. The match's sound sinks are for effects and speech; MUSIC_HAP is a separate channel, and giving the adapter one would mean inventing a music subsystem rather than translating a routine.

_note: seam_audit.py keys on a seam's NAME, so one declared in several
callback structs and filled in only one of them reads as filled.
check_secret_moves was exactly that and had to be found by hand.
The tool reports the shape as a heuristic -- declared in more
structs than it has assignment sites -- and these are the
explanations for the names it currently flags. Underscore-prefixed
so the two-way guard on the real ledger ignores it: these names ARE
filled, so they are not empty seams and must not be rows above.
_PARTIAL.get_health: Declared in wm_arcade_react1_core.h, where it is filled, and in wm_arcade_getup_meter.h, where it is deliberately optional. The getup meter takes it because WRESTLE2.ASM:1074 calls get_health exactly there, and passing NULL changes no answer: the low-health arm falls through into the same GETUP_TIME test the high-health arm reaches, so the suppression its comment describes was never assembled. test_getup_meter sweeps health 0..100 and asserts the answer never moves, which is why this one is demonstrated rather than asserted.
_PARTIAL.play_sound: Declared in wm_arcade_react1_core.h, where it is filled, and in wmania_attract_adapter.h and wmania_hiscore_adapter.h, where it is not. Those two are the frontend screens' own sound, and every other seam in both adapters is ledgered display or hardware for the same reason -- there is no renderer for the screens the sound would accompany. Consistent with the show_* rows above rather than a separate decision.
